extracted.intended_audience: reporters and journalism students who cover meetings, legislative hearings, and investigations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing news stories about public meetings, legislative sessions, committee investigations, and hearings—how to select, shape, and present proceedings for newspaper readers. Focuses on purpose, treatment, and techniques (including handling testimony and human-interest phases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story — meetings/investigations as a distinct class
rubrics_metrics.description: News stories of various kinds of meetings constitute a distinct class. In the term 'meeting' are included sessions of state legislatures, meetings of municipal councils, conventions of various organizations, and meetings of local societies. Investigations and hearings as conducted by committees of legislative bodies are also placed in this class, although they are often more like judicial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify the assignment correctly: treat ordinary meetings as the 'informative type' (focus on parts of proceedings of general interest and significance). Recognize when an investigation/hearing requires judicial-style handling. Use appropriate story form depending on the type and importance of the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — accuracy and completeness as significance warrants
rubrics_metrics.description: To give the facts accurately and as completely as their significance warrants should be the first aim in reporting proceedings of official bodies, because, like court proceedings, they are matters of public concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize factual accuracy and include all matters whose significance justifies it; avoid omissions that undercut public understanding. Balance comprehensiveness with news judgment: include detail to the extent the significance warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on distortion or suppression for advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The desire to accomplish some end, no matter how laudable that end may be, does not justify distortion or suppression of the news of the doings of official bodies. A constructive purpose, such as that of exposing sinister influences that may be affecting legislative action, is entirely justifiable, but distortion or suppression of facts in order to make out a stronger case is not legitimate and should not be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reshape facts to advance a cause. Investigative zeal is permitted but must not lead to misrepresentation. Political partisanship that misrepresents public matters harms the paper's reputation and the public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show significance to readers — contextualize public acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Much more effort should be made by newspapers in this country to show the significance of acts of representative public bodies, in relation not only to the home and business interests of the individual reader, but to the welfare of the community, the state, and the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why measures matter to readers: connect proceedings to local/home interests and broader civic consequences. Provide clear exposition of the meaning and likely effects of decisions or debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — make dry proceedings interesting
rubrics_metrics.description: To make interesting what is often considered dry and unattractive in proceedings of various public meetings, is the chief problem in writing news stories concerning them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simple, clear explanation of significant parts, lively accounts of debate, and vivid description of persons and scenes to add interest. Employ human-interest, humorous or pathetic phases legitimately to heighten interest and emphasize significance, but avoid sensationalizing trivial incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and prioritize the vital matters
rubrics_metrics.description: To select the vital matters, to present them concisely, and to condense routine but necessary details into the smallest possible compass in stories of this class, require effort and skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the core issues and outcomes; pare routine procedural minutiae to the essentials. Lead with what is most significant and condense background and routine details to brief summarizing sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid playing up insignificant incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Too often, however, insignificant incidents of casual interest are played up as features of meetings of importance to the subordination or even to the exclusion of matters of vital concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist the temptation to emphasize amusing or quirky sidelines at the expense of substantive acts. Use anecdotes sparingly and only when they illuminate or underscore the main point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle testimony like court stories when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony in investigations and hearings sometimes has dramatic phases like that in court trials. The questions and the answers in these proceedings are handled like those in court stories, and testimony is dealt with in much the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting testimony, use the same techniques as in courtroom reporting: select vivid exchanges, paraphrase lengthy Q&A while preserving meaning, quote salient declarations, and note demeanor and dramatic moments that affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use human-interest and humor legitimately for lesser meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Some meetings lend themselves to humorous treatment, and when the news interest in them is slight, such stories about them constitute typical human interest stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For meetings of limited public consequence, choose a human-interest or lighter angle to engage readers. Ensure the tone matches the importance and avoid trivialization when stakes are substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condense routine details and present concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: To select the vital matters, to present them concisely, and to condense routine but necessary details into the smallest possible compass in stories of this class, require effort and skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice tight editing: summarize procedural aspects, eliminate redundancy, and use compact paragraphs. Preserve essential context but cut filler so readers get the gist quickly.
